correctness.rationale: Inspected every analytic estimate: reciprocal summability ensures compact-uniform convergence of G(w)=prod_j(1-w/s_j)^2 and log H(T)=o(T) for H(T)=prod_j(1+T/s_j) by dominated convergence. For |w|=s_j, the exp(w) maximum angular loss has a quadratic lower bound in |w-s_j|; the double zero of G provides an upper perturbation proportional to the same square. Because B_j=R_j(2/s_j+4)e^(-s_j)H(s_j)^2 tends to zero, a single positive epsilon makes all off-root inequalities strict. On w=s_j the perturbation vanishes, giving exactly n maxima; f'(0)=epsilon, upper e^(r^n)+o(e^(r^n)) and lower values at R_j give exact order n/type 1. The s_j=(j+1)(log(j+2))^2 sequence is reciprocal-summable and yields the claimed near-power lower count. All quantifiers are analytic and no finite truncation is used as proof.

originality.rationale: The closest earlier works prescribe maximum-modulus discontinuity radii for an entire function or individual maximum points at different radii, often with geometric separation to retain finite order. These are not equivalent to exactly n simultaneous global maxima at every arbitrarily dense reciprocal-summable prescribed radius, with first Taylor exponent one, exact order and type and near-power exceptional count. Li proves generic two-point bound outside a locally finite exceptional set but no upper density on that set. The double-zero perturbation idea has antecedents, which are credited. This is best-of-knowledge originality, not priority certainty.
residual_risks: Double-zero perturbation constructions are a known technique; an older specialized infinite simultaneous maxima interpolation statement might imply a special case.
The theorem gives a sufficient reciprocal-summability condition, not a necessary characterization or optimal exceptional-radius density.

value.rationale: There is a substantive tension between the generic maximum-count bound set by the first Taylor gap and unrestricted exceptional-radius accumulation toward infinity. The theorem shows near-power frequency of n-fold exact global maximizing sets with complete growth control and no geometric separation, a motivated sharp qualitative strengthening of prior exceptional-circle existence.

final_claim: For any n>=3 and increasing s_j→infinity with sum 1/s_j finite, an explicit entire f with f(0)=1, f'(0) nonzero, order n and exponential type 1 has exactly the n n-th-root positions as global maximizers on all circles |z|=s_j^(1/n). Some such f have at least c_n R^n/(log R)^2 exceptional radii <=R where more than two maxima occur.
limitations: Order n>=3 fixed, reciprocal-summable strictly increasing prescribed s_j and no claims beyond the specified circles; no Eremenko–Lyubich class B guarantee.
